parallel.requirements: Recognized the requested Ligra graph framework evolution: Paper 1 framework primitives, applications, Ligra+ compression support, runner, results, and patches.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Created parent task records for applications, commit/patch work, compression headers, compressed vertices/tools, and final runner/results, then delegated the applications through a background workflow.
parallel.implementation: Produced substantial partial implementation through children: multiple apps and partial compression/header work appeared in the workspace, with child reports for builds and sanity checks.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Did not reconcile the workflow outputs into the required final delivery path; the runner/results requirement remained unsatisfied.
parallel.verification: Component-level child verification existed in the workflow journal, but no parent-level end-to-end acceptance run consumed it.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final evaluated workspace still had the placeholder run.sh and zero completed requirements after timeout.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Ligra and Ligra+ task obligations from the prompt and framework TODOs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept work in one local actor with no subagents or workflow calls, writing only a high-level plan before continuing investigation.
serial.implementation: Did not reach meaningful implementation beyond planning and reading framework sections in the completed attempt.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No integrated runner, results file, or requirement patch was delivered by the serial run.
serial.verification: No meaningful whole-task verification occurred before timeout; evaluator observed the placeholder runner.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final evaluated workspace still had the placeholder run.sh and zero completed requirements after timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the broad Ligra and Ligra+ obligations and explicitly created work items for applications, compression headers, compressed vertices, and the final runner/results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also recognized the broad task and wrote a plan, but reached only local reading and planning before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed recognized requirements into delegated implementation work; serial kept the requirements local and made much less implementation progress.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent created explicit task records and launched a workflow with app-level children for implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had no delegation and no subagents, with the main actor retaining all implementation responsibility.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used distributed ownership through workflow children; serial was a single-owner local attempt.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow brief supplied detailed file boundaries, build commands, framework facts, and per-application requirements to the children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept context in the main trajectory, reading framework sections and then planning direct implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The contrast is not a missing brief or interface contract; parallel children received substantial context, while serial avoided handoff boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel workflow produced several app implementations and local app verification reports, and the parent later saw many app files and partial compression headers in the workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt wrote an agent plan and then continued reading framework TODOs; it did not reach comparable implementation output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel made materially more component implementation progress, while serial largely remained in survey/planning.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child workflow recorded implementation and verifier results, but protocol validation shows the workflow was not retrieved without stop.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no child result lifecycle because actual_parallel_used is false.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The distinctive parallel failure is an unjoined delegated result lifecycle; serial lacks that coordination boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote into the shared workspace, and the parent observed untracked app files, copied headers, and compression headers, but no final runner was assembled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced only local planning artifacts and no comparable shared multi-agent integration state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had partial shared implementation state needing a parent join; serial had ordinary incomplete local state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow children reported app-level builds/runs and independent checks, but those checks did not become end-to-end acceptance for the submitted runner.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run did not reach meaningful end-to-end verification and the evaluator found the same placeholder runner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had trapped component verification; serial had little verification because implementation never matured.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed many requests/tools, recorded workflow protocol failure, and closed after all three outer-loop rounds with zero completed requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also exhausted the official agent timeout but with far fewer tools and no delegation protocol failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out; parallel closure carried an additional unresolved workflow-join failure while serial closure was a local incomplete attempt.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current official evaluations completed and failed with agent_timeout, so there is no discordant outcome. The meaningful difference is that the parallel run generated partial delegated implementation and verification artifacts but failed to join them into a final runner, while the serial run stayed mostly in local planning and investigation. The shared official failure is explained by the same delivered-state fact: run.sh remained the placeholder in both modes.
parallel_contributors: Background workflow implementation results were not joined into the final deliverable before closure.
serial_contributors: The single-agent attempt made little implementation progress and also never replaced the placeholder runner.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel produced several app files and component checks; serial primarily produced a plan and framework reads.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized parallel-side adverse process consequence only

candidates.reason: Rejected: implementation ownership existed through app and compression tasks plus the parent; the problem was not absence of an implementer.
Rejected: no concrete incompatible multi-component integration episode is shown; the direct failure is the unjoined workflow result and missing final runner.
Rejected: final assembly was explicitly assigned by the Write run.sh and results.json task, so the deliverable was owned even though it was not completed.
Rejected: the parent maintained the end-to-end task list and workflow; this is an incomplete join/closure episode, not a missing pipeline owner.
Rejected: productive implementation was not blocked behind a single serial preflight; multiple implementation children ran and produced files/results.
Rejected: the parallel run did not defer all productive work until after an investigation phase; it launched implementation children directly.
Rejected: there is no separately evidenced underallocation of the indispensable path; the specific observed boundary is the missing workflow join.
Rejected: broad fan-out and timeout are visible, but the concrete adverse episode is non-retrieval/non-join, not proven collective budget exhaustion.
Rejected: the delegated app work was split across app-level children; no single child is shown to be overbroad and uniquely blocking closure.
Rejected: the workflow brief included task, file, build, verification, and delivery context; no omitted known requirement drove unusable child work.
Rejected: per-file ownership and app boundaries were specified, and no observed incompatible cross-agent interface required unplanned reconciliation.
Rejected: no known information is shown disappearing through a summary or transfer; the issue is a workflow result that was not joined.
Rejected: child reports may be long, but there is no evidence the parent received them and failed to reduce their volume before acting.
Rejected: no consumed handoff described a superseded workspace, requirement, dependency, or decision state.
Rejected: no incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated.
Rejected: the parent did not make an observable whole-task completion decision; closure was a timeout with the runner still placeholder.
Rejected: no replacement or retry repeated prior work because it lacked inherited checkpoints or current state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Rejected: there is no parent stop/cancel/interrupt of a needed active child before finalizing its work.
Rejected: there was no complete directly promotable final candidate; core deliverables such as run.sh were still absent.
Rejected: no child result was integrated only after relevant integrated verification; the result was not joined into a final verified runner.

A background workflow performed delegated application implementation and recorded completed child results, but the parent did not retrieve or join the workflow result before closure. The final evaluator still encountered the placeholder runner, making the lost join a realized adverse parallel-side process consequence.
candidates.realized_consequence: Delegated application work and workflow-local verification were not reconciled into the final deliverable, so the submitted workspace still had the placeholder run.sh.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did not receive and ignore a concise completed result; the observed failure is that the workflow result stayed below the required parent join boundary.

candidates.reason: Rejected: verifier findings are part of the same trapped workflow lifecycle as the delegated implementation, so the more direct retained label is Missing Implementation Join.
Rejected: no required child failure, abort, or cancellation is the direct event; the problem is a completed/retrievable workflow not joined.
Rejected: no concise completed result is shown visible to the parent and ignored; protocol instead records that the workflow was not retrieved without stop.
Rejected: the parent did inspect workspace progress, including git status and app files; the direct failure was not a blind wait.
Rejected: multiple files were written, but there is no observed competing design or overlapping behavior conflict needing reconciliation.
Rejected: no live agents are shown editing the same source/configuration file and forcing reconciliation.
Rejected: no agent is shown replacing or deleting source produced or actively owned by another agent.
Rejected: the required runner stayed placeholder; no concurrent actor overwrote a submitted entry point or executable deliverable.
Rejected: no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced a current final tree and invalidated another actor's work.
Rejected: agents shared a workspace, but no concrete unstable state or provenance failure distinct from the missing join is proven.
Rejected: no generated cache, fixture, temp file, or auxiliary artifact from one actor was consumed by another as stable input.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: A background workflow performed delegated application implementation and recorded completed child results, but the parent did not retrieve or join the workflow result before closure. The final evaluator still encountered the placeholder runner, making the lost join a realized adverse parallel-side process consequence.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Delegated application work and workflow-local verification were not reconciled into the final deliverable, so the submitted workspace still had the placeholder run.sh.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The parent did not receive and ignore a concise completed result; the observed failure is that the workflow result stayed below the required parent join boundary.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Missing Verifier Return was suppressed because verifier findings were trapped in the same workflow result lifecycle as the retained implementation join episode.
Fan-out Budget Exhaustion and Blind Timeout Wait were suppressed because timeout symptoms do not add a distinct allocation or wait episode beyond the missing join.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no other candidate had a separate episode, consequence, and evidence set.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Only the directly evidenced workflow join boundary was retained to avoid relabeling the same timeout/result lifecycle as multiple patterns.
